reason: Codex called it blocking; claude called the same thing a migration residual. Codex is right: --collect REPLAYS an already-paid review off the journal rather than convening it twice, so a run journalled before the fix comes back with seats = everyone who ANSWERED, and cycle 2 taught the renderer to read that tuple as reporters. The original overclaim therefore survived for a supported operation on a run the operator already paid for. REDESIGNED on codex proposal, which also dissolves claude separate residual that the RAN/UNAVAILABLE overload was documented rather than typed: seats now means one thing on every status (who answered) and a new reporting field carries the readable subset. None means NOT RECORDED and the header states that limit instead of guessing past it; () is what unreadable_output carries and is refused on RAN. Journal writes reporting even when None, and the reader distinguishes an ABSENT key from a null one via a _MISSING sentinel because dict.get collapses them. Verified end-to-end through journal -> replay -> header for legacy, degraded and full-panel records; the full-panel line is byte-identical, so the fixture and eval 1 are untouched. Added 3 tests (legacy replay, RAN-with-empty-reporting refused, reporter-not-in-seats refused).
